Overview

About the All-Flash NVMe Storage

Supermicro Petascale servers are all-flash NVMe storage systems built around EDSFF E3.S drives. A symmetrical layout keeps signal paths short and airflow even, so they can feed GPU clusters and AI data pipelines with high throughput and low latency.

They are used as the building block for software-defined and parallel file systems, and are available with Intel Xeon, AMD EPYC or NVIDIA Grace CPU Superchip processors.

E3.S all-flash

Up to 16 E3.S drives in 1U or 32 in 2U.

Petabyte scale

Hundreds of terabytes in 1U and up to a petabyte in 2U with high-capacity drives.

PCIe 5.0 and DDR5

Twice the I/O bandwidth of PCIe 4.0 for GPU data feeds.

CXL memory

1U models support E3.S 2T bays for CXL memory modules.

Grace option

NVIDIA Grace CPU Superchip models for energy-efficient software-defined storage.

Specifications

Technical Specifications

1U Petascale

Drive baysUp to 16 hot-swap E3.S, or 8 E3.S plus 4 E3.S 2T (CXL)
CapacityUp to 256 TB with current E3.S Gen 5 drives

2U Petascale

Drive baysUp to 32 hot-swap E3.S
CapacityUp to about 0.5 PB, rising to 1 PB with 30 TB-class drives
SocketsSingle- and dual-processor models

Platform

CPUsIntel Xeon, AMD EPYC or NVIDIA Grace CPU Superchip, per model
I/OPCIe 5.0
MemoryDDR5
Example modelSSG-222B-NE3X24R
